findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year" vs. "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Specify whether returning employees begin a fresh benefit year or return to their original eligibility window (e.g., "Returning employees begin a new benefit-year cycle on their first day back" or "their benefit-year clock remains tied to their original hire date").
findings.location: Eligibility section, "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.violation: It's unclear whether employees returning from leave restart their benefit-year clock or retain their original timeline. This creates ambiguity about how many claims they can make in their actual calendar year.

findings.evidence: "the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing"
findings.fix: Reorder as: "The stipend request moves to final processing once both the manager signs and finance confirms the budget line."
findings.location: How to Apply section, second paragraph beginning "Also, the stipend request..."
findings.violation: The sequence of events is unclear and possibly backwards - it's ambiguous whether the manager signs before or after finance review.

findings.evidence: "The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Remove "Then" and move this sentence before "The employee receives a confirmation email," or reword to: "The employee reviews the confirmation summary and submits final approval."
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph beginning "Then, the employee reviews..."
findings.violation: The timeline is illogical - the employee cannot review the confirmation and then submit the request if processing has already finished and the confirmation has already been sent.

findings.evidence: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives."
findings.fix: Reword as: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the requester supplies the missing documentation."
findings.location: Approval Timeline section, third paragraph beginning "An incomplete request..."
findings.violation: "Missing item" is misleading when the request itself is incomplete (lacking documentation). It conflates missing information with undelivered equipment.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Reword as: "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition. The benefits team may request a brief photo verification once per year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first paragraph
findings.violation: Switches from third-person policy language to second-person ("you," "we"), inconsistent with the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there..."
findings.fix: Clarify roles separately (e.g., "The employee records..." / "The manager countersigns..." / "The requester tracks...") and avoid second person throughout.
findings.violation: Multiple inconsistencies - shifts between second person ("you"), unclear subject for "countersign," and mixing of employee and manager roles without clarity.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Reword as: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: Grammatically parallel structure is broken - "confirming eligibility" (gerund) pairs awkwardly with "the uploaded receipt" (noun phrase).

findings.evidence: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate or consolidate the sections.
findings.violation: This sentence is identical to one in the Program Overview section.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.location: Program Coordination section, third and fourth sentences
findings.violation: These sentences are entirely unrelated to home-office equipment stipend policy and should not be in this document.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Specify the condition (e.g., "flags any duplicate request submitted within the same quarter" or "flags any second request for the same equipment category within the same quarter").
findings.violation: "Repeats" is vague - does it mean a duplicate request, a second claim for the same category, or the same equipment item?

findings.evidence: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.location: Questions and Updates section, second sentence
findings.violation: This statement is identical to one in the Program Overview section.
